study: Taylor et al. (2015), BSCS Science: An Inquiry Approach curriculum + curriculum-based PD, efficacy trial, Am. Educ. Res. J.
eval_evidence: Study conducted/authored by BSCS staff (all authors at Biological Sciences Curriculum Study), who 'were also developers of the curriculum materials.' IES-funded (R305K060142 to BSCS) but developer-conducted, not an independent third-party contractor.
developer_evidence: The PD was delivered by 'PD facilitators from BSCS'; 'two of the developers of An Inquiry Approach were also on the' PD team. The developing organization (BSCS) itself delivered the curriculum-based PD to teachers.
cascade_evidence: BSCS PD facilitators delivered the seven-day/year PD (3-day summer institute + four one-day sessions) directly to the treatment teachers; no train-the-trainer or lead-teacher cascade described.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison schools used 'business-as-usual materials planned by their schools and districts' — one of eight different textbooks in Grade 9, progressing to their usual Grade-10 programs. Standard BAU contrast; no shared branded program or assessment contaminating control.
coaching_evidence: PD = 3-day summer institute + four one-day group sessions during the year (off-site/group workshop-institute format). Classroom observations were conducted only to measure fidelity (RTOP), not as ongoing in-class coaching. No in-class coaching cycles -> none.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes only the teacher's regular science instruction (the An Inquiry Approach curriculum enacted in class); no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose added.
maturity_evidence: Primary outcome measured spring of Grade 10 after TWO years of program implementation (Grades 9 then 10); pupils/teachers had a full prior implementation year (Grade 9) before the Grade-10 measurement wave -> measured after >=1 prior year.
